scientific_role: Post-hoc negative control of the second-independent-Agent-session explanation; not confirmatory effect estimation.

case_results.interpretation: A2 independently reproduced the inability to locate legitimate providers for engine.FWObject and connection.common.FWConnection. It rejected source edits and synthetic modules, then submitted a no-op program that Official failed. Neither a second free session nor replay repaired this case.

Without online clean-replay feedback, a second independent strong-Agent session found a reconstructible legacy compatibility path, passed the post-session nonfeedback clean qualification, and independently Official-passed. The B success is therefore not exclusive to replay.

infrastructure_adjudication.host_repair: Installed the previously missing git-lfs system package on Spark. The final endpoint used the exact unchanged input on another registered ARM64 host after repeated Spark network censoring.

hypothesis_decision.killed_claim: The screen15 result demonstrates that same-session clean replay increases terminal success relative to an equally strong free-Agent control.
hypothesis_decision.reason: On the complete preidentified opportunity set, B and an equal second free-Agent session produced the same repairs and the same screen-level Official success. The only B success was also achieved without replay.

strongest_support_remaining: B can operationally return complete-program clean-replay counterexamples inside one active session and did produce an eligible Official-passing repair after A1 failed.
strongest_counterevidence: The same case Official-passed under a second no-replay Agent session, so ordinary session variability fully explains the observed terminal gain.

next_experiment.design: Select a larger outcome-blind consumed/Dev cohort before new outcomes. Run A1 on every case. For every A1 eligible complete-program Official failure, run both A2 and qualified B in randomized order under the same model and evaluation conditions.
next_experiment.primary_contrast: Count B-exclusive wins (B Pass, A2 Fail) against A2-exclusive wins (A2 Pass, B Fail); both-pass outcomes do not establish replay gain.
next_experiment.falsification_rule: If B has no reproducible exclusive terminal wins over A2, kill replay as the EnvSolve-Pro core algorithm rather than adding rules.

claim_limits: One A2 replicate on two opportunities is enough to refute the simple unique-gain interpretation of screen15, but not enough to estimate stochastic pass probabilities or the population effect of replay.
safeguard_policy: No new hash, frozen contract, or software gate was added.
